name: THREE.MeshLine
role: Thick camera-facing lines for Three.js; npm three.meshline, pmndrs fork is meshline
summary: Replacement for THREE.Line that draws lines as strips of camera-facing triangles, so width, dashes and taper work where WebGL lines are fixed at one pixel. Supplies MeshLine geometry, MeshLineMaterial and raycast. Two packages exist: three.meshline from the original author (2.0.0, 2026) and meshline, the pmndrs fork used by R3F (3.3.1, 2024).
use_when: Over THREE.Line when width, dashes or taper must render consistently across devices
Animated stroke reveals via dashOffset or visibility as a function of t
Stylised trails and orbit lines in a Three.js scene
avoid_when: Flat 2D stroke animation: SVG with GSAP or Paper.js
Screen-space lines without a separate package: Line2 in Three.js examples/jsm

evidence.result: 90 alpha frames at 1280x720, 90 distinct hashes; shuffled order matches sequential; frame 45 alpha min 0 max 1; expected/summary.json diff passed three 0.186.1, Chromium 156.0.8078.4, Playwright 1.64.1, Node 22.19.0, screenshot route.
evidence.scope: MeshLine + MeshLineMaterial lines (lineWidth, color, dashOffset, visibility, rebuilt points) per seek in three.js; headless Chromium, macOS arm64; no pmndrs fork.

notes: 2026-10-26: the earlier catalogue install of meshline is the pmndrs fork; the original now publishes as three.meshline. The 2026 README says the pmndrs fork exists; whether it will track r155+ changes was not verified.

assessment.rationale: Original spite repo is live again: three.meshline 2.0.0 published 2026-10-13, needs three r155+. The pmndrs fork (npm meshline) last released Jun 2024 and is slow, so prefer three.meshline.
